lesson_title: Debtors Control: The Account That Checks Itself
hook_text: Forty customers owe you money. One account tells you the total — and catches errors.
clip_script: Here is the principle you must hold onto for the whole lesson: whatever is posted to the individual debtors' accounts in detail must be posted to the control account in total. Detail in the Debtors Ledger, totals in the control account — two views of the same facts. That gives us the built-in check that makes this topic the backbone of reconciliation questions in every grade: at month end, the balance of the Debtors Control account must equal the total of the list of individual debtors' balances. If the summary and the detail disagree, an error exists, and it must be hunted down. This is internal control in action — the books policing themselves.
visual_style: Split screen: forty small personal accounts on one side merging into a single bold control account on the other, with a green tick when the totals match.
pacing: Quick setup, deliberate emphasis on the agreement rule, punchy close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and post the whole month yourself.
